claims.statement: Binary Shannon entropy is uniquely maximal at sigma=1/2, with value ln 2.
Equal-gain normalized two-channel cancellation occurs only at sigma=1/2 and relative phase pi.
The fixed set of J(s)=1-conjugate(s) is Re(s)=1/2.
Entropy deficit from balance equals Bernoulli KL divergence and is positive away from 1/2.
Within the binary-spinor model, complement symmetry, maximal entropy, spinorial sign and phase-locked cancellation are equivalent to sigma=1/2.
Eta and zeta have identical zero sets with multiplicity in the open critical strip.
Unequal channel gains shift the cancellation point to |b|^2/(|a|^2+|b|^2).
A canonical regular, covariant and gauge-independent zeta-state map converts every non-trivial zero into equal-gain complementary cancellation.
Under SOH-C001 and the channel hypotheses, every non-trivial zero lies on Re(s)=1/2.
A theta-kernel, analytic-vector, positivity or reproducing-kernel construction satisfies the canonical bridge requirements.
A self-adjoint operator has a spectral determinant proportional to Xi.
The native paired theta state satisfies P(J(s)) = X conjugate(P(s)).
The normalized native PhaseNav closure defect equals (Re(s)-1/2)^2.
The continuous paired theta-Mellin detector equals xi(s).
Every non-trivial xi zero closes in the canonical self-dual PhaseNav shell.
Under SOH-C004, every non-trivial zero lies on Re(s)=1/2.
The 18-pair detector is a low-height quadrature approximation to xi(s).
For an involution-fixed finite centred zero fixture, the PhaseNav-Weil matrix reduces to a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix.
The declared two-channel Gaussian profile detects a synthetic off-axis quartet through a negative minimum eigenvalue.
The complete arithmetic PhaseNav-Weil operator is positive on a dense admissible test-channel family and its null structure forces native closure.
Under SOH-C005 and the exact Weil correspondence, every non-trivial zero lies on Re(s)=1/2.
The Gaussian PhaseNav-Weil matrix test has the declared closed Fourier transform under the exp(-2 pi i x r) convention.
The declared prime-side matrix is stable between the two prime cutoffs and matches the low-height spectral receipt.
Finite spans of translated-scaled Hermite PhaseNav channels are dense in Schwartz space.
The Hermite kernel has the declared closed Fourier transform and Hhat_mn(0)=delta_mn.
PSD of every finite Hermite section plus continuity extends non-negativity to the dense core.
The finite Hermite ladder through basis size six is cutoff-audited and PSD-tested.
Binary complement is conjugate to reciprocal inversion in projective odds coordinates.
The unique positive reciprocal fixed point corresponds to p=1/2.
p=1/2 is the Fisher-Rao geodesic midpoint between the labelled pure states.
DEFINED_ZERO and UNDEFINED_BOTTOM are interpreted as informational boundary labels; IEEE NaN is not a numeric endpoint.
The logarithmic prime tail is compactified by z_tail=1/log(x) to a finite interval with a smooth flat endpoint.
Every fixed Hermite entry has the declared upper-incomplete-gamma prime-tail majorant under an explicit monotonicity condition.
Entrywise prime-tail certificates imply a finite-section operator-norm bound and Weyl eigenvalue enclosure.
For w=0.8, Q=100000 and N<=6, the largest certified prime-tail operator-norm bound is 7.717202888999335e-13.
For every c>0, the basis-adaptive schedule Q_N=exp(cN) forces the declared coarse Hermite finite-section prime-tail envelope to zero.
For w=0.8, Q0=100000, log Q_N=max(log Q0,2N), and N<=20, all sharp certificates pass 1e-12, with maximum 3.280365246530569e-14 at N=5.
